name: Slagpatch Acid-Proof Shelf Poncho
description: A rough rectangle of salvaged industrial tarp stitched with mismatched cord, coated in layers of recycled rubberized sealant gone yellowy-grey from repeated acid exposure. Crude hood tunnel is reinforced with a strip of salvaged conveyor belting. Worn, patched, and faintly chemical-smelling — but it keeps the acid rain off chrome and skin alike.
functionality: Full-torso acid rain barrier with reinforced hood; crude chrome-pass slits cut into sides for basic arm augmentations.
what_it_says: Survival first, aesthetics never — this person is fighting the Shelf one rainstorm at a time.
story_hooks: The poncho has a serial number stamped on the tarp — from a sealed Ferrochem waste shipment that was never supposed to reach the Shelf.
Someone stitched a small map into the inner lining in orange thread. It leads somewhere underground.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian, shapeless poncho with an aggressive industrial aesthetic. The garment drapes loosely over the shoulders in an irregular rectangle, creating a deliberately crude silhouette. The hood tunnel protrudes forward like a bunker, giving the wearer a hunched, defensive posture. Patched and re-patched across its surface, it reads as worn armor rather than fashion.
physical_description.fit: Oversized and deliberately formless, designed for maximum coverage over layers and augmentation. No tailoring—just drape and bulk. The hood is pull-on, friction-fit over the head. Worn loose enough to slip over loaded webbing or bulky shoulder mods.
physical_description.primary_material: Salvaged industrial tarp (polyvinyl or PVC blend) heavily coated in recycled rubberized sealant—the kind used for warehouse sealing and structural waterproofing. Conveyor belting reinforces seams and hood.
physical_description.texture: Thick and plasticky with a slightly tacky feel from accumulated chemical residue. Surface is cratered and dulled from repeated acid rain exposure. Seams are rough, knotted with mismatched cord (nylon, paracord, electrical wire). Visible patches of degradation and repair create an intentionally weathered, almost scaled appearance.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominantly yellowy-grey with darker grey panels and charcoal reinforcement strips. Brownish stains and white chemical burn marks scattered across the surface. No attempt at coherence—pure functional patching.
physical_description.closures: None. Pull-on hood design. The poncho simply drapes; worn over clothing or harness.
distinctive_features: Conveyor belt strip running around hood perimeter for reinforcement
Visible mismatched stitching in contrasting cord colors
Randomly placed acid-damage patches and burn marks
Faint chemical residue smell (acrid, metallic undertone)
Multiple layers of sealant visible at worn edges
Asymmetrical patching showing years of field repair
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 salvage / sub-grade. This is not purchased; it is scavenged, inherited, or bartered in underground markets.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street worker, industrial salvager, acid-rain zone commuter, or someone operating in ungoverned areas where protection from environmental hazards matters more than appearance. Signals survivalism and indifference to social hierarchy. The wearer has normalized danger.
physical_description.condition_typical: Always weathered and patched. New condition would be suspicious. A worn-in, chemically stained Slagpatch is a functional tool that proves its owner works outside corporate climate controls.
